Subject: Post-demo: Telemetry & marketplace data-sharing follow-up

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on related to telemetry, marketplace flows, and third-party sharing: 

1) What we log: Redwood does not persist full request text as part of telemetry by default. We capture request metadata (model, token counts, latency, error codes) and coarse event telemetry for routing/health.
2) PII handling: We recommend customers remove or token-hash PII before calling the hosted API. For customers who need to send PII, we offer Private deployments with customer-managed keys and on-prem options.
3) Marketplace flows: When using cloud marketplace billing providers, minimal transaction metadata is shared with the marketplace vendor (invoice id, non-sensitive usage counters). We do not share prompt/response payloads with marketplace partners.
4) Subprocessors: core subprocessors include AWS (compute/storage), CloudObservabilityCo (telemetry ingestion), and DocuSign for contracts. We provided a subprocessors list during the call; attaching a one-page data map and a .xlsx matrix for deeper fields.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll upload the detailed data map + retention matrix (attached).
- Laura will send an engineer note about the telemetry pipeline and whether KV cache or user identifiers ever appear in logs.
- Schedule a 30-min security sync with your SecOps (suggest Wed 5/5 midday).
- I’ll include a redline of our standard agreement for procurement to review.

Attachments: redwood_data_map_v1.pdf, data_handling_matrix.xlsx, contract_redline_v1.docx

If that aligns, I’ll send calendar invites.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Telemetry & marketplace data-sharing follow-up

Olivia — appreciate the questions. Short answers up front, more details below and Laura will follow with the engineering note.

- CloudObservabilityCo only receives anonymized event streams (no user-emails/IDs by default). We emit hashed IDs for dedup/metric continuity; hashes are salted per-customer and rotate on a 90-day cadence.
- Marketplace partners receive billing metadata (usage counters, invoice id, aggregated daily totals). They do not receive timestamps linked to request-level payloads or prompt text.
- Default retention: 90 days for detailed telemetry, 13 months for aggregated billing/usage. We can contractually reduce detailed telemetry retention to 30 days for enterprise Private deployments.

Attached: redwood_data_map_v1.pdf (data map), data_handling_matrix.xlsx (column-level mapping). Also linking SOC2 report via drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-data-map

I’ve penciled 11:30am PT on Wed 5/5 for a 30-min SecOps sync; please confirm attendee list so we can add a dial-in.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Telemetry & marketplace data-sharing follow-up

Hi Olivia — adding the engineering detail as promised. Short technical summary: 

- Telemetry pipeline: In hosted mode, request-level traces are processed in an isolated ingestion cluster. Sensitive fields are redacted via configurable scrubbing rules before storage. By default we remove fields matching email, SSN, credit-card patterns and drop anything flagged by the customer scrubbing config.
- KV cache: the runtime K/V cache is ephemeral in memory and not written to persistent telemetry stores. Cache hit/miss counters are emitted as aggregated metrics only.
- Marketplace flows: during marketplace provisioning we emit a provisioning event (customer_id, region, SKU). That event is stored as aggregated metadata; payloads and prompt/response pairs are never transmitted to billing partners.
- Subprocessor specifics: CloudObservabilityCo is used only for metric ingestion and alerting; logs (text) are stored in AWS S3 under customer-specific prefixes if the customer opts in. For Private deployments we can configure S3 to point to customer-managed buckets.

If helpful, I can produce a short CSV mapping field -> where it flows (telemetry, billing, logs) and whether it can contain PII. I attached the matrix that maps common fields and suggested retention policy.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
